answers.explanation: Buffer async work between batch and worker = SQS. night-13-sqs-decoupling.md decision tree. SNS is push fan-out; Step Functions is orchestration.
Visibility timeout must exceed max processing time (or use ChangeMessageVisibility / Lambda event source mapping). Classic exam trap.
Monthly Iceland completions — order irrelevant, throughput matters → standard queue. FIFO when order/dedup required (Q9 contrast).
RedrivePolicy + DLQ isolates poison messages after maxReceiveCount failed processing cycles. night-13-lab-sqs-setup.sh defaults.
EventBridge → SQS needs queue resource policy with events.amazonaws.com and aws:SourceArn = rule ARN. sqs-completion-queue-policy.json.
Long polling (WaitTimeSeconds up to 20) cuts empty ReceiveMessage churn. night-13-lab-sqs-consumer.sh uses 20s.
Single worker tier pulling from SQS = buffer + back-pressure. SNS fans out pushes; does not consolidate to one queue consumer pattern.
DLQ without redrive policy does nothing useful. maxReceiveCount on source queue required.
Per-customer ordering + dedup → FIFO with MessageGroupId + content-based deduplication. Standard queue wrong for ledger.
At-least-once: message hidden during visibility timeout, then visible again if not deleted. Flashcard #2.
Schedule trigger (Night 12) vs completion handling (Night 13 SQS) — loose coupling split. Multiple rules on default bus are fine.
SQS is Regional. Cross-Region queue access is possible but usually wrong for latency/cost — queue near consumer or replicate events.
ApproximateNumberOfMessages is eventually consistent — do not treat as exact ledger count.
Event pattern filters exit 0 only — failed Iceland run produces no completion message. Add failure path via SNS in Night 14.
SNS fan-out to many subscribers — Night 14 preview. SQS + Lambda works but one queue ≠ multi-subscriber push.
